payload.tier_rubric:
# Conservative admission-tier rubric (conservative-v1.1)

Every applicable hard check must pass or be explicitly not applicable before a formal recommendation. Unknown is not a pass. Separate eligibility, tuition budget, goal fit and admission risk.

For reviewed, program-specific cohort counts from the latest three admission cycles:

- Lottery: offers / applications <= 15%.
- Reach: offers / applications > 15% and <= 35%.
- Above 35%: aggregate counts alone do not establish a tier.

These are explicit engineering thresholds for cohort-selectivity planning labels, not university classifications, calibrated predictions, or an applicant's personal admission probability. Cite the counts, cycle and source; mention that applicant pools and future admissions can differ. Use `comparison_dimensions=["selectivity"]` for this route. Satisfying minimum conditions does not imply competitiveness. Do not call a cohort-based recommendation personalized odds.

Target requires at least two independent, recent, traceable admitted cases from the same degree/track, with comparable original GPA scale/scope and relevant academic/experience background. Safer requires the same evidence and a supported explanation of relatively lower risk. Safer never means guaranteed. Aggregated rates cannot substitute for these cases. Duplicate copies count once; no automatic GPA conversion or inferred experience is allowed. Semantic comparisons need human review.

Goal-fit claims need bound official curriculum, internship, capstone or thesis evidence. Never infer placement from school reputation. Recommend the few fully supported candidates even when other tiers are empty. Keep other non-failing candidates pending. At most five recommendations per tier; explain shortages below three. Do not guarantee admission, scholarships, employment or visas.

sources.fact_summary: Fall 2027 application rules: GPA 3.0, GRE, transcripts, CV, SOP and three letters. Program curriculum includes an internship and capstone. Video requirements differ by program.

sources.title: MSAII FAQ: admission criteria and undergraduate background
sources.locator: MSAII FAQ: admission criteria and undergraduate background
sources.source_excerpt: a strong background in computer science and mathematics
sources.fact_summary: A bachelor-level background and strong undergraduate computer science and mathematics preparation are expected, including for non-CS majors. Published legacy TOEFL minimum 100 or IELTS 7.5; GRE is required without a score cutoff. Intake-specific validity dates come from current central admissions.

sources.title: SCS admissions: Test Scores / English Language Proficiency
sources.locator: SCS admissions: Test Scores / English Language Proficiency
sources.fact_summary: For Fall 2027, English tests before September 1, 2024 are not accepted for applicants without US degree study; qualifying US degree study permits September 1, 2021 onward. This is not an English-test waiver.

sources.title: MSAII admitted-student information: Tuition and fees
sources.locator: MSAII admitted-student information: Tuition and fees
sources.fact_summary: Department-specific 2026–2027 tuition is USD 32,400 per academic semester. Four academic semesters plus required summer course: 6–12 units at USD 650/unit. Total tuition estimate USD 133,500–137,400.

sources.fact_summary: MSAII 2025 cohort: 526 applications and 58 offers. Year is identified by the comparison-page column group; exact counts come from its official JSON datasource. Cohort statistics do not describe an individual applicant probability.

sources.fact_summary: The comparison table labels applications and admitted counts as 2025. Selectivity means offers divided by applications; program requirements influence the applicant pool.
